core_meaning.primary_meaning: Salsal (صَلْصَال) is a Qur'anic masculine given name meaning 'pure resounding clay' or 'the wondrous substance of creation'. It is directly attested in the Holy Qur'an in Surah al-Rahman (55:14) and Surah al-Hijr (15:26, 28, 33) describing the primordial material from which Allah created humanity before breathing into it the spirit of life.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Dry, pure clay that produces a clear, resonant sound when touched, signifying cohesive strength, purity, and the marvel of divine craftsmanship.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: In Surah al-Rahman (55:14), Allah declares: 'خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ' ('He created man from clay like that of pottery'). Classical commentators such as Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari explain that salsal represents pure clay that has dried until it resounds, illustrating the profound Quranic truth that humble earthly dust is elevated through divine will into conscious, noble beings.
